finalModules.title: 转机与行程调整
finalModules.focus: 核对时间、条件和替代路线，而不是只听单个数字

vocab.head: connection
vocab.example: Our connection in Berlin was delayed, so we had time to check the information desk before choosing another route.
vocab.exampleZh: 我们在柏林的接驳延误了，所以有时间先问服务台再选路线。

vocab.head: departure
vocab.example: The departure board showed a new gate, but it did not explain whether the boarding time had also changed.
vocab.exampleZh: 出发显示屏换了登机口，却没说明登机时间是否改变。

vocab.head: confirm
vocab.example: I asked an assistant to confirm the time because my phone was still showing the original booking details.
vocab.exampleZh: 我请工作人员确认时间，因为手机仍显示原预订信息。

vocab.head: available
vocab.example: Two seats were available on an evening flight, although we would reach the hotel much later than planned.
vocab.exampleZh: 晚班机有两个座位，不过我们会比计划晚很多到酒店。

vocab.head: alternative
vocab.example: The assistant suggested an alternative involving a train journey to a nearby airport and a shorter final flight.
vocab.exampleZh: 工作人员提出另一选择：坐火车去附近机场，再乘较短的最后一程航班。

vocab.head: luggage
vocab.example: Our luggage had already been checked in, so we needed to know whether it could travel with us.
vocab.exampleZh: 行李已经托运，所以我们需要知道能否随我们同行。

vocab.head: transfer
vocab.example: She could transfer our bags, but only if we accepted the new route before the next check-in deadline.
vocab.exampleZh: 她能转运行李，但前提是我们在下一次值机截止前接受新路线。

vocab.head: deadline
vocab.example: The deadline gave us twenty minutes to decide, which was enough to compare the arrival times carefully.
vocab.exampleZh: 截止前有二十分钟，够我们仔细比较到达时间。

vocab.head: direct
vocab.example: A direct train from the first airport would arrive later than the flight, but it offered fewer changes.
vocab.exampleZh: 从第一个机场坐直达火车会比飞机晚到，但换乘较少。

vocab.head: priority
vocab.example: My sister’s priority was avoiding another missed connection rather than arriving as early as possible that evening.
vocab.exampleZh: 姐姐优先考虑避免再错过接驳，而不是当晚尽早抵达。

vocab.head: arrange
vocab.example: We asked the hotel to arrange a late arrival and chose the train because its timetable felt more reliable.
vocab.exampleZh: 我们请酒店安排晚到，并因时刻表更可靠而选择火车。

vocab.head: receipt
vocab.example: We kept every receipt in case the airline later asked for evidence of the extra costs we had paid.
vocab.exampleZh: 我们保留每张收据，以防航空公司后来要求额外费用凭证。

sourceA.title: 转机与行程调整：教学情境
sourceA.text: Our connection in Berlin was delayed, so we had time to check the information desk before choosing another route. The departure board showed a new gate, but it did not explain whether the boarding time had also changed. I asked an assistant to confirm the time because my phone was still showing the original booking details. Two seats were available on an evening flight, although we would reach the hotel much later than planned. The assistant suggested an alternative involving a train journey to a nearby airport and a shorter final flight. Our luggage had already been checked in, so we needed to know whether it could travel with us. She could transfer our bags, but only if we accepted the new route before the next check-in deadline. The deadline gave us twenty minutes to decide, which was enough to compare the arrival times carefully. A direct train from the first airport would arrive later than the flight, but it offered fewer changes. My sister’s priority was avoiding another missed connection rather than arriving as early as possible that evening. We asked the hotel to arrange a late arrival and chose the train because its timetable felt more reliable. We kept every receipt in case the airline later asked for evidence of the extra costs we had paid.

sourceB.title: A ferry after a cancellation
sourceB.text:
Ravi and his friend planned to take a ferry to an island on Friday afternoon. At the harbour they learned that their sailing had been cancelled because of strong winds. The next ferry might leave on Saturday morning, but staff could not guarantee it. Ravi wanted to wait because they had already booked a room on the island. His friend suggested staying in the coastal town instead.
Before deciding, they contacted the island hotel. The owner explained that guests whose ferry was cancelled could move their booking without an extra charge, provided they called before six that evening. The friends also checked the last bus to the coastal town, which left at five forty.
They chose the bus and moved their hotel booking to the following weekend. This meant changing their plans, but it avoided spending the night at a harbour with no confirmed departure. On the bus, Ravi admitted that his first choice had been based mainly on not wanting to lose the room. Once they knew the hotel’s conditions, they could make a calmer decision using the information actually available.

listening.teaching: Hello, this is Leila from Greenway Coaches. You booked a seat on tomorrow’s nine o’clock service to the lake. Road repairs mean the coach will now leave from the west side of the station rather than the usual entrance. The departure time is unchanged. Please arrive fifteen minutes early because the temporary stop is a short walk from the ticket office. Your ticket remains valid, and there is no need to print a replacement. If you have difficulty walking, call us this afternoon so the driver can explain a closer meeting point. The return journey will use the normal stop because the repairs should be finished by then.
listening.test: Good afternoon. I am calling about your bicycle reservation for Saturday’s hill train. Passenger seats are still available, but the bicycle space you requested cannot be confirmed on the ten o’clock service. We can carry both you and your bike on the eleven thirty departure. Alternatively, you may keep your original passenger seat and hire a bicycle after you arrive. The hire shop is beside the destination station, although its charge is not included in your train ticket. Please reply by four today. If we do not hear from you, we will keep the passenger booking and cancel only the unconfirmed bicycle request.

questions.prompt: Why did the travellers ask about luggage?
options: The hotel needed the flight number.
The train charged separately for every bag.
It had already been checked in.
questions.answer: It had already been checked in.
questions.explanation: 原文说明已托运，须确认行李能否转运。

questions.prompt: Why did they choose the train?
options: It would reach the hotel earlier.
Avoiding another missed connection mattered most.
It avoided contacting the hotel again.
questions.answer: Avoiding another missed connection mattered most.
questions.explanation: 姐姐的重点是减少接驳风险而非最早到达。

questions.prompt: What changed about the coach?
options: Its departure stop.
Its departure time.
Its return stop.
questions.answer: Its departure stop.
questions.explanation: 西侧临时站代替原入口，时间没变。

questions.prompt: Who should call the coach company?
options: Passengers wanting to print a replacement ticket.
Passengers joining the return coach.
Passengers who have difficulty walking.
questions.answer: Passengers who have difficulty walking.
questions.explanation: 提前联系可获得更近集合点说明。

questions.prompt: What did the island hotel allow?
options: Keeping the original room until Saturday without calling.
Moving the booking after a ferry cancellation.
Receiving transport from the harbour at no charge.
questions.answer: Moving the booking after a ferry cancellation.
questions.explanation: 只要六点前联系，可改期且无额外费。

questions.prompt: Why was Ravi initially reluctant to change plans?
options: He did not want to lose the booked room.
He expected the coastal town to be more expensive.
He thought the bus would miss its last departure.
questions.answer: He did not want to lose the booked room.
questions.explanation: 他承认原决定主要怕损失房间。

questions.prompt: What can be confirmed at eleven thirty?
options: A bicycle on the original ten o’clock departure.
Bicycle hire included in the rail price.
Travel with the bicycle.
questions.answer: Travel with the bicycle.
questions.explanation: 十一点半有乘客及自行车空间。

questions.prompt: What happens without a reply?
options: Both seat and bicycle booking move to eleven thirty.
The passenger seat stays, but the bike request is cancelled.
The passenger seat is cancelled but the bike request remains.
questions.answer: The passenger seat stays, but the bike request is cancelled.
questions.explanation: 留言明确区分乘客座位与未确认自行车请求。

writing.prompt: Write a message to a hotel explaining a travel delay. State your expected arrival, ask about late check-in and explain what you still need to confirm.
checklist: 回应题目要求，包含具体情境与明确目的。
用段落或清楚顺序组织信息，补充必要原因。
检查时态、指代及词语搭配，避免影响理解的错误。
核对内容是否由自己独立组织，并说明信息的来源。

speaking.prompt: Compare two travel alternatives after a cancellation, explaining your priorities.
followups: Why would that choice suit this situation?
What difficulty might occur?
How would you explain the situation to someone who disagrees?

interaction.goal: 选择一条可行路线并明确行李、费用和时间条件。
interaction.twist: 服务人员告知最早路线需要再次换乘，另一条晚到但直达。

delayed.readingPrompt: At least fourteen days later, read a new account of a similar problem. Identify its purpose, two important details and one difference from this module.
delayed.writingPrompt: Write a new message about a similar situation with different people and constraints. Do not reuse the original wording.
delayed.speakingPrompt: Explain a fresh solution to a partner, then answer two unexpected follow-up questions without a script.

assessmentWriting.prompt: Write to the island hotel explaining your cancelled ferry, the booking change you want and the condition you need confirmed.
checklist: 包含陌生情境要求的信息与明确目的。
给出具体理由或条件，不照搬教学任务的答案。
组织顺序清楚，检查指代、时态与礼貌程度。
独立完成并保留原稿，交给伙伴或教师核对是否易懂。

assessmentSpeaking.prompt: Discuss the ferry travellers’ decision. Explain which new information made changing plans more reasonable.
followups: Which condition matters most in this particular situation?
What would you ask before agreeing?
How would you respond if the other person suggested a different solution?

finalModules.title: 住宿问题与礼貌协商
finalModules.focus: 清楚描述问题、提出合理请求并核对解决条件

vocab.head: reservation
vocab.example: When we reached the guesthouse, our reservation was on the system, but the room described in the email was unavailable.
vocab.exampleZh: 我们到旅馆时系统有预订，但邮件描述的房间没空。

vocab.head: ground floor
vocab.example: We had requested a ground floor room because my father found long flights of stairs difficult after an operation.
vocab.exampleZh: 我们要求地面层房间，因为父亲术后难爬长楼梯。

vocab.head: receptionist
vocab.example: The receptionist apologised and showed us a larger room upstairs, without first checking whether there was a working lift.
vocab.exampleZh: 接待员道歉，带我们看楼上更大的房，却没先检查电梯是否正常。

vocab.head: access
vocab.example: I explained that easy access mattered more to us than extra space or a view across the garden.
vocab.exampleZh: 我解释通行方便比额外空间或花园景色更重要。

vocab.head: temporary
vocab.example: She offered a temporary room beside the dining area while the manager checked arrangements at a nearby guesthouse.
vocab.exampleZh: 她提供餐区旁的临时房，让经理去查附近旅馆安排。

vocab.head: disturb
vocab.example: We asked whether breakfast preparation would disturb my father early in the morning, since he needed plenty of rest.
vocab.exampleZh: 我们问早餐准备是否会一早打扰父亲，因为他需要充足休息。

vocab.head: explain
vocab.example: The manager listened carefully and explained that the neighbouring building had an accessible room available for the whole stay.
vocab.exampleZh: 经理认真听后解释，隔壁建筑全程都有无障碍房。

vocab.head: additional
vocab.example: There would be no additional payment, and the guesthouse would organise transport for our bags rather than expect us to carry them.
vocab.exampleZh: 无需额外付费，旅馆会安排运包，而不是让我们自己搬。

vocab.head: agreement
vocab.example: Before accepting the agreement, I checked that breakfast and the final night were included, just as in our original booking.
vocab.exampleZh: 接受约定前，我核对早餐及最后一晚都像原订单一样包含。

vocab.head: written
vocab.example: We requested written confirmation so that staff at the other building would understand the arrangements when we arrived later.
vocab.exampleZh: 我们要求书面确认，让另一建筑员工稍后接待时懂安排。

vocab.head: solution
vocab.example: The solution was not our first choice, but it met the important need that the larger upstairs room could not.
vocab.exampleZh: 解决办法不是首选，却满足楼上大房不能满足的重要需求。

vocab.head: patient
vocab.example: Remaining patient helped us keep the discussion focused on practical needs instead of repeating how disappointed we felt that afternoon.
vocab.exampleZh: 保持耐心帮助我们聚焦实际需求，而非反复表达当天下午多失望。

sourceA.title: 住宿问题与礼貌协商：教学情境
sourceA.text: When we reached the guesthouse, our reservation was on the system, but the room described in the email was unavailable. We had requested a ground floor room because my father found long flights of stairs difficult after an operation. The receptionist apologised and showed us a larger room upstairs, without first checking whether there was a working lift. I explained that easy access mattered more to us than extra space or a view across the garden. She offered a temporary room beside the dining area while the manager checked arrangements at a nearby guesthouse. We asked whether breakfast preparation would disturb my father early in the morning, since he needed plenty of rest. The manager listened carefully and explained that the neighbouring building had an accessible room available for the whole stay. There would be no additional payment, and the guesthouse would organise transport for our bags rather than expect us to carry them. Before accepting the agreement, I checked that breakfast and the final night were included, just as in our original booking. We requested written confirmation so that staff at the other building would understand the arrangements when we arrived later. The solution was not our first choice, but it met the important need that the larger upstairs room could not.

sourceB.title: A noisy holiday apartment
sourceB.text:
Marta rented an apartment near a market because the description promised a quiet place for remote work. On the first morning, building work began in the apartment above. She contacted the owner and explained that she had online meetings for three afternoons. The owner said the repairs were urgent but offered a refund for the unused nights.
Marta did not accept immediately. Finding another apartment at short notice would take time, and she liked the location. She asked whether there was a quiet room elsewhere in the building that she could use during meetings. The owner checked with a neighbour who managed a small office on the ground floor.
They agreed that Marta could use the office from one until five, when it was normally empty. The arrangement did not stop the morning noise, but it protected the part of her stay that mattered most. She asked the owner to update the listing for future visitors. A helpful solution to her own difficulty did not remove the need to tell other guests about the repair work before they booked.

listening.teaching: Welcome to Willow House. Breakfast is usually served from seven to nine, but guests joining the early walking tour may collect a packed breakfast from reception at six thirty. Please tell us by eight this evening if you want one. The kitchen cannot prepare individual requests after that time. Water bottles can be filled from the tap beside the dining room; there is no charge. The front door locks automatically at ten at night, so take your room card if you go out. If the card stops working, use the bell on the left of the door rather than the one marked delivery. A member of staff is available overnight.
listening.test: Hello, this is the manager of River Rooms. You asked whether you could leave your bags with us after checkout tomorrow. We can store them until six in the evening, but reception will close between one and two while staff attend training. If you need to collect the bags during that hour, please tell us tonight so we can arrange access through the café next door. There is no storage fee. We cannot leave valuable items unattended, however, so please keep passports and small electronic devices with you. The taxi you requested is confirmed for five thirty, and the driver will meet you at the main entrance.

questions.prompt: What mattered most to the family?
options: A quieter view across the garden.
More space for the same price.
Easy access for the father.
questions.answer: Easy access for the father.
questions.explanation: 父亲术后不便爬楼，通行优先。

questions.prompt: Why request written confirmation?
options: To ask the manager to extend their stay.
To make the transfer arrangements clear to other staff.
To change the breakfast time.
questions.answer: To make the transfer arrangements clear to other staff.
questions.explanation: 书面信息避免另一处接待误解。

questions.prompt: When must packed breakfast be requested?
options: By eight this evening.
By seven tomorrow morning.
By nine this evening.
questions.answer: By eight this evening.
questions.explanation: 留言给出明确截止时间。

questions.prompt: Which bell should a locked-out guest use?
options: The bell marked delivery.
The bell inside the dining room.
The bell on the left.
questions.answer: The bell on the left.
questions.explanation: 门卡失效时用左侧铃。

questions.prompt: Why did Marta hesitate over the refund?
options: The office was too far from the apartment.
Moving would take time and she liked the location.
The owner had refused to offer money back.
questions.answer: Moving would take time and she liked the location.
questions.explanation: 退款并不直接解决换房成本。

questions.prompt: What did Marta want future listings to mention?
options: The repair work.
The availability of a free permanent office.
The number of online meetings she personally held.
questions.answer: The repair work.
questions.explanation: 个人妥协不代替对后续客人如实说明。

questions.prompt: When will reception be closed?
options: Between five thirty and six.
Between noon and one.
From one until two.
questions.answer: From one until two.
questions.explanation: 员工培训导致一到二点关闭。

questions.prompt: What should guests keep with them?
options: Identification only after collecting the taxi.
Passports and small electronic devices.
Large bags that cannot fit in the café.
questions.answer: Passports and small electronic devices.
questions.explanation: 贵重小件不进入无人看管寄存。

writing.prompt: Write a polite email about a room that does not meet an important booking requirement. Explain the requirement and request two possible solutions.
checklist: 回应题目要求，包含具体情境与明确目的。
用段落或清楚顺序组织信息，补充必要原因。
检查时态、指代及词语搭配，避免影响理解的错误。
核对内容是否由自己独立组织，并说明信息的来源。

speaking.prompt: Describe a booking problem and negotiate a practical remedy without exaggerating.
followups: Why would that choice suit this situation?
What difficulty might occur?
How would you explain the situation to someone who disagrees?

interaction.goal: 明确核心需求并确认转房费用及服务。
interaction.twist: 经理提供更大房间，但它仍不满足行动不便者的通行需求。

delayed.writingPrompt: Write a new message about a similar situation with different people and constraints. Do not reuse the original wording.
delayed.speakingPrompt: Explain a fresh solution to a partner, then answer two unexpected follow-up questions without a script.

assessmentWriting.prompt: Write to an apartment owner about a noisy stay during remote work. Propose a remedy other than moving immediately.
checklist: 包含陌生情境要求的信息与明确目的。
给出具体理由或条件，不照搬教学任务的答案。
组织顺序清楚，检查指代、时态与礼貌程度。
独立完成并保留原稿，交给伙伴或教师核对是否易懂。

assessmentSpeaking.prompt: Negotiate a quiet workspace while recognising that urgent building repairs may continue.
followups: Which condition matters most in this particular situation?
What would you ask before agreeing?
How would you respond if the other person suggested a different solution?

finalModules.title: 身体不适与清楚求助
finalModules.focus: 准确报告症状、时间与既有情况，核对专业人员指示

vocab.head: unwell
vocab.example: During our walking holiday, my cousin felt unwell and decided to stop before the group reached the next village.
vocab.exampleZh: 徒步度假时表弟身体不适，决定不到下一村就停下。

vocab.head: symptom
vocab.example: He described each symptom to the tour leader instead of simply saying that everything felt wrong that afternoon.
vocab.exampleZh: 他逐项向领队描述症状，而不只说那天下午哪儿都不舒服。

vocab.head: dizzy
vocab.example: He felt dizzy when standing up, although he had not fallen or hit his head on the path.
vocab.exampleZh: 他站起时眩晕，不过没有跌倒或在路上撞头。

vocab.head: appointment
vocab.example: The leader called a local clinic and asked whether an appointment was available before its normal closing time.
vocab.exampleZh: 领队打电话问当地诊所正常关门前是否有预约。

vocab.head: describe
vocab.example: A staff member asked him to describe when the problem began and whether it had happened on earlier walks.
vocab.exampleZh: 工作人员让他描述何时开始及以前徒步是否发生过。

vocab.head: allergy
vocab.example: He mentioned an allergy to a medicine and showed the name saved on his phone to avoid a misunderstanding.
vocab.exampleZh: 他提到一种药物过敏，并展示手机保存的药名避免误会。

vocab.head: insurance
vocab.example: I found his travel insurance details while the leader arranged transport, rather than leaving him to manage everything alone.
vocab.exampleZh: 领队安排交通时我找到旅行保险资料，不让他独自处理一切。

vocab.head: instructions
vocab.example: At the clinic, he asked for the instructions in writing because he was worried about forgetting important details later.
vocab.exampleZh: 在诊所他要求书面指示，担心稍后忘记重要细节。

vocab.head: repeat
vocab.example: The nurse was willing to repeat unfamiliar words, and he checked his understanding by explaining the main points back.
vocab.exampleZh: 护士愿意重复生词，他通过复述要点核对理解。

vocab.head: contact
vocab.example: She also explained whom to contact if his condition changed, without expecting the tour leader to make a medical judgement.
vocab.exampleZh: 她还说明情况变化时联系谁，而不让领队作医学判断。

vocab.head: recover
vocab.example: He stayed near the village to recover and followed the clinic’s advice instead of trying to finish the original route.
vocab.exampleZh: 他留在村附近恢复并遵从诊所建议，而非尝试走完原路线。

vocab.head: support
vocab.example: Practical support meant listening and helping him reach professional care, not guessing a diagnosis from our own experiences.
vocab.exampleZh: 实际帮助是倾听并协助就医，而非根据自身经验猜诊断。

sourceA.title: 身体不适与清楚求助：教学情境
sourceA.text: During our walking holiday, my cousin felt unwell and decided to stop before the group reached the next village. He described each symptom to the tour leader instead of simply saying that everything felt wrong that afternoon. He felt dizzy when standing up, although he had not fallen or hit his head on the path. The leader called a local clinic and asked whether an appointment was available before its normal closing time. A staff member asked him to describe when the problem began and whether it had happened on earlier walks. He mentioned an allergy to a medicine and showed the name saved on his phone to avoid a misunderstanding. I found his travel insurance details while the leader arranged transport, rather than leaving him to manage everything alone. At the clinic, he asked for the instructions in writing because he was worried about forgetting important details later. The nurse was willing to repeat unfamiliar words, and he checked his understanding by explaining the main points back. She also explained whom to contact if his condition changed, without expecting the tour leader to make a medical judgement. He stayed near the village to recover and followed the clinic’s advice instead of trying to finish the original route.

sourceB.title: A dental appointment abroad
sourceB.text:
While visiting a friend overseas, Hana developed tooth pain that kept returning during meals. She searched for a nearby dental clinic and phoned rather than relying only on its booking website. The receptionist asked when the pain had started and whether she had received recent dental treatment. Hana explained that she was a temporary visitor and wanted to know the likely appointment cost before confirming.
The clinic could offer a check the following morning. It could not promise the full treatment price before a dentist examined her. Hana asked whether she could receive a written estimate before agreeing to any further work. The receptionist confirmed that this was possible and asked her to bring identification and details of any regular medication.
Hana wrote down the address, time and cancellation condition. She also checked the route because the clinic entrance was on a side street rather than the main road shown on the map. Her friend offered to accompany her. Hana accepted the help, while making clear that she wanted to answer the dentist’s questions herself and ask for explanations whenever something was unclear.

listening.teaching: Hello, this is Lakeside Medical Centre confirming your appointment at ten twenty tomorrow. Please arrive ten minutes early to complete a short form. Bring identification and a list of any medicines you currently take, including their names if you know them. You do not need to send private health information by ordinary email before you arrive. If you require an interpreter, please call reception today so we can check availability; bringing a friend does not always replace professional interpreting. The centre entrance is beside the pharmacy, but the pharmacy itself does not handle appointments. If you cannot attend, contact reception as soon as possible so another patient can use the time.
listening.test: This is a reminder from Oak Street Dental Clinic. Your appointment on Wednesday is at two fifteen, not two fifty as stated in our earlier message. We apologise for the error. The dentist will examine the problem first and discuss possible treatment and charges before you decide whether to continue. Please do not assume the examination fee covers every later procedure. If you have previous dental records available, you may bring them, but your appointment will still go ahead without them. The lift is temporarily out of service. Anyone who cannot use the stairs should telephone us before travelling so we can discuss an accessible arrangement.

questions.prompt: Why did the cousin show a name on his phone?
options: To show the insurance payment.
To confirm the walking route.
To make the medicine allergy clear.
questions.answer: To make the medicine allergy clear.
questions.explanation: 药名展示减少过敏信息误解。

questions.prompt: How did he check his understanding?
options: By asking the leader to explain a diagnosis.
By explaining the main instructions back.
By reading only the appointment time.
questions.answer: By explaining the main instructions back.
questions.explanation: 复述是核对理解而非自诊。

questions.prompt: Why arrive early for the medical appointment?
options: To complete a form.
To collect a medicine before the clinic opens.
To speak to the pharmacy receptionist.
questions.answer: To complete a form.
questions.explanation: 要求提前十分钟填表。

questions.prompt: What should someone needing an interpreter do?
options: Ask a friend to arrive without informing reception.
Send a private medical history by ordinary email.
Call reception today.
questions.answer: Call reception today.
questions.explanation: 需要先核查口译人员可用性。

questions.prompt: What could the dental clinic not promise by phone?
options: The cost of the first appointment itself.
The full treatment price before examination.
Whether identification was needed.
questions.answer: The full treatment price before examination.
questions.explanation: 检查后才能明确完整治疗费用。

questions.prompt: Why did Hana check the route?
options: The entrance was on a side street.
The published opening time had changed.
The map showed the wrong town.
questions.answer: The entrance was on a side street.
questions.explanation: 地图主路不等于实际入口。

questions.prompt: What was corrected in the dental reminder?
options: The examination fee.
The day of the appointment.
The appointment time.
questions.answer: The appointment time.
questions.explanation: 两点十五取代两点五十。

questions.prompt: Who should call before travelling?
options: Someone without earlier dental records.
Someone unable to use stairs.
Someone who has not paid for treatment in advance.
questions.answer: Someone unable to use stairs.
questions.explanation: 电梯故障，需要无障碍安排者应提前联系。

finalModules.title: 购买、退换与售后
finalModules.focus: 区分商品问题、个人偏好及退换条件

vocab.head: purchase
vocab.example: I took a recent purchase back to the outdoor shop after discovering that its zip caught whenever I closed the jacket.
vocab.exampleZh: 我发现夹克拉链每次拉上会卡，就把最近购买的物品带回户外店。

vocab.head: faulty
vocab.example: The assistant asked me to show why I thought the fastening was faulty rather than simply choosing the wrong size.
vocab.exampleZh: 店员让我展示为何认为扣件有问题，而非只是选错尺寸。

vocab.head: receipt
vocab.example: I had kept the receipt, which showed the purchase date and made it easier to find the original transaction.
vocab.exampleZh: 我保留收据，上有购买日期，更容易找到原交易。

vocab.head: exchange
vocab.example: An exchange seemed practical because I still liked the jacket and wanted one that worked for the walking trip.
vocab.exampleZh: 换货似乎实际，因为我仍喜欢夹克，想要一件徒步时能正常用的。

vocab.head: replacement
vocab.example: Before accepting a replacement, I tested its zip several times and checked that the pocket seams were properly closed.
vocab.exampleZh: 接受替换品前，我多试几次拉链，并检查口袋缝线收好。

vocab.head: stock
vocab.example: The same colour was not in stock, but the shop could order it from another branch within four days.
vocab.exampleZh: 同色没有库存，但店里能四天内从另一分店调来。

vocab.head: deadline
vocab.example: My travel deadline was sooner than that, so waiting for the preferred colour would not meet my immediate need.
vocab.exampleZh: 我的出行时间更早，等待喜欢的颜色无法满足眼前需要。

vocab.head: refund
vocab.example: The assistant explained a refund option, although I wanted to compare it with taking a different colour that afternoon.
vocab.exampleZh: 店员解释退款选项，不过我想与当天下午拿其他颜色比较。

vocab.head: condition
vocab.example: I asked whether the sale price changed any condition of the proposed exchange and listened carefully to the explanation.
vocab.exampleZh: 我问促销价是否改变换货条件，并仔细听解释。

vocab.head: decision
vocab.example: My decision depended on a working jacket for the trip, not on proving that every part of the shopping experience was bad.
vocab.exampleZh: 我的决定取决于旅途有能用的夹克，不是证明购物经历处处糟糕。

vocab.head: confirm
vocab.example: We agreed on another colour, and the assistant gave me a new receipt to confirm exactly what had been exchanged.
vocab.exampleZh: 我们同意换另一颜色，店员给新收据确认具体换了什么。

vocab.head: reasonable
vocab.example: A reasonable solution came from describing the fault clearly and explaining the practical problem caused by the delivery times.
vocab.exampleZh: 合理解决来自清楚描述故障，并解释配送时间造成的实际困难。

sourceA.title: 购买、退换与售后：教学情境
sourceA.text: I took a recent purchase back to the outdoor shop after discovering that its zip caught whenever I closed the jacket. The assistant asked me to show why I thought the fastening was faulty rather than simply choosing the wrong size. I had kept the receipt, which showed the purchase date and made it easier to find the original transaction. An exchange seemed practical because I still liked the jacket and wanted one that worked for the walking trip. Before accepting a replacement, I tested its zip several times and checked that the pocket seams were properly closed. The same colour was not in stock, but the shop could order it from another branch within four days. My travel deadline was sooner than that, so waiting for the preferred colour would not meet my immediate need. The assistant explained a refund option, although I wanted to compare it with taking a different colour that afternoon. I asked whether the sale price changed any condition of the proposed exchange and listened carefully to the explanation. My decision depended on a working jacket for the trip, not on proving that every part of the shopping experience was bad. We agreed on another colour, and the assistant gave me a new receipt to confirm exactly what had been exchanged.

sourceB.title: A repair instead of a return
sourceB.text:
Omar bought a small speaker for listening to language lessons. After three weeks, the charging connection became loose. He contacted the seller and explained that the sound still worked, but the battery would not charge reliably. The seller asked for a short video showing the problem and offered to arrange a repair.
Omar first wanted an immediate replacement because he used the speaker every day. However, the seller explained that the repair centre could inspect it within two days and lend him another unit while he waited. Before accepting, Omar asked who would pay the delivery charges and what would happen if the fault could not be repaired. He received those details in writing.
The speaker returned a week later with a replaced connection and a repair record. Omar tested it before sending back the borrowed unit. He was pleased with the result but suggested that the seller should explain the repair process more clearly on its website. Customers would be less anxious if they knew the likely timetable and available temporary support before having to complain about a fault.

listening.teaching: Thanks for contacting City Cameras about your order. The lens you requested is available, but the carrying case is delayed. You can choose to receive the lens tomorrow and the case next week, with no second delivery charge. Alternatively, we can hold the complete order until both items are ready. Please tell us which you prefer before three this afternoon. If you need the case for a trip this weekend, we can cancel that item and refund its cost without changing your lens order. The case shown in the alternative photograph is a different size, so we do not recommend it for this lens.
listening.test: Hello, I am calling from the repair desk about your watch. The inspection found a damaged strap fitting rather than a battery problem. We can replace the fitting, but we need your agreement because this repair is outside the service package you bought. The charge is written in the email we sent today. Please reply to that email or call us before Friday. If you decide not to continue, we will return the watch unrepaired and you will pay only the inspection charge already agreed. We will not carry out extra work simply because we have the watch here. Your original strap is being kept safely with it.

questions.prompt: What evidence helped the shop find the transaction?
options: The jacket’s repair history.
A photograph of the shop window.
The receipt.
questions.answer: The receipt.
questions.explanation: 收据含日期，可查购买记录。

questions.prompt: Why not wait for the preferred colour?
options: The preferred colour cost more.
The trip began before it could arrive.
The shop had already ordered the wrong size.
questions.answer: The trip began before it could arrive.
questions.explanation: 时间限制比颜色更重要。

questions.prompt: What can the customer receive tomorrow?
options: The lens without the delayed case.
The lens together with the requested case.
A suitable alternative case at the same price.
questions.answer: The lens without the delayed case.
questions.explanation: 镜头可先送，包下周送且无第二次运费。

questions.prompt: Why is the alternative case not recommended?
options: It would arrive after the trip.
It came with a separate delivery charge.
It is a different size.
questions.answer: It is a different size.
questions.explanation: 尺寸不适合该镜头。

questions.prompt: What temporary support did Omar receive?
options: A refund before the inspection.
A borrowed speaker during the repair.
A replacement speaker to keep permanently.
questions.answer: A borrowed speaker during the repair.
questions.explanation: 借用设备解决日常使用中断。

questions.prompt: What did Omar confirm before accepting?
options: Delivery charges and the outcome if repair failed.
Whether he could change the speaker’s colour.
Whether the seller would refund his lessons.
questions.answer: Delivery charges and the outcome if repair failed.
questions.explanation: 明确费用及不能修复时安排。

questions.prompt: What caused the watch problem?
options: An old battery.
Damage to the original strap itself.
A damaged strap fitting.
questions.answer: A damaged strap fitting.
questions.explanation: 检查区分了故障来源。

questions.prompt: What happens if extra work is declined?
options: The shop completes the repair and charges later.
The watch returns unrepaired under the agreed inspection charge.
The inspection charge is automatically removed.
questions.answer: The watch returns unrepaired under the agreed inspection charge.
questions.explanation: 未经同意不开展收费额外维修。

writing.prompt: Write a clear after-sales message about a faulty product. Explain the fault, evidence, preferred remedy and a practical time limit.
checklist: 回应题目要求，包含具体情境与明确目的。
用段落或清楚顺序组织信息，补充必要原因。
检查时态、指代及词语搭配，避免影响理解的错误。
核对内容是否由自己独立组织，并说明信息的来源。

speaking.prompt: Negotiate a repair, replacement or refund while checking cost and timing.
followups: Why would that choice suit this situation?
What difficulty might occur?
How would you explain the situation to someone who disagrees?

interaction.goal: 选定能满足实际需要的售后方案并确认条件。
interaction.twist: 最喜欢的替换品不能及时送达，但可提供临时借用品。

finalModules.title: 问路与无障碍出行
finalModules.focus: 根据实际通行条件理解方向，不把最近当作最合适

vocab.head: route
vocab.example: A visitor asked me for a route to the museum while we were waiting outside the station.
vocab.exampleZh: 一位游客在车站外等候时向我问去博物馆的路线。

vocab.head: entrance
vocab.example: The nearest entrance was beside a narrow bridge, but I knew there were several steps beyond it.
vocab.exampleZh: 最近入口在窄桥旁，但我知道后面有几级台阶。

vocab.head: wheelchair
vocab.example: His daughter used a wheelchair, so I asked whether he wanted a step-free route before giving directions.
vocab.exampleZh: 他女儿用轮椅，所以指路前我问是否需要无台阶路线。

vocab.head: crossing
vocab.example: I suggested the crossing with traffic lights rather than the shorter path through a busy car park.
vocab.exampleZh: 我建议走有信号灯的过街处，而非穿越繁忙停车场的近路。

vocab.head: opposite
vocab.example: The museum’s accessible gate was opposite the library, which was easy to recognise by its yellow doors.
vocab.exampleZh: 博物馆无障碍门在图书馆对面，黄门很容易认。

vocab.head: straight ahead
vocab.example: I told him to go straight ahead after the crossing until he reached the small public garden.
vocab.exampleZh: 我让他过马路后一直向前，到小公共花园。

vocab.head: turn
vocab.example: There he should turn left, keeping the garden on his right until the library came into view.
vocab.exampleZh: 那里左转，把花园留在右侧，直到看到图书馆。

vocab.head: distance
vocab.example: The extra distance was modest, although the route would probably take longer than the map first suggested.
vocab.exampleZh: 多走距离不大，不过路线可能比地图起初显示耗时长。

vocab.head: surface
vocab.example: He asked about the surface because rough stones had made the previous afternoon’s walk surprisingly difficult.
vocab.exampleZh: 他问路面情况，因为昨天下午的粗石路让行走意外困难。

vocab.head: check
vocab.example: I offered to check the museum website in case construction had temporarily changed the accessible entrance.
vocab.exampleZh: 我提出查官网，以防施工临时改变无障碍入口。

vocab.head: explain
vocab.example: Before leaving, he repeated the main turns so I could explain anything that still sounded unclear.
vocab.exampleZh: 离开前他重复主要转弯，让我解释仍不清楚之处。

vocab.head: confident
vocab.example: He felt more confident with a suitable route than with a quick promise that everything was nearby.
vocab.exampleZh: 合适路线比一句一切就在附近的快速保证更让他有把握。

sourceA.title: 问路与无障碍出行：教学情境
sourceA.text: A visitor asked me for a route to the museum while we were waiting outside the station. The nearest entrance was beside a narrow bridge, but I knew there were several steps beyond it. His daughter used a wheelchair, so I asked whether he wanted a step-free route before giving directions. I suggested the crossing with traffic lights rather than the shorter path through a busy car park. The museum’s accessible gate was opposite the library, which was easy to recognise by its yellow doors. I told him to go straight ahead after the crossing until he reached the small public garden. There he should turn left, keeping the garden on his right until the library came into view. The extra distance was modest, although the route would probably take longer than the map first suggested. He asked about the surface because rough stones had made the previous afternoon’s walk surprisingly difficult. I offered to check the museum website in case construction had temporarily changed the accessible entrance. Before leaving, he repeated the main turns so I could explain anything that still sounded unclear. He felt more confident with a suitable route than with a quick promise that everything was nearby.

sourceB.title: Finding a temporary library
sourceB.text:
A town library moved into a former school while its main building was repaired. The online map still directed visitors to the old entrance, so the temporary staff placed notices at both locations. Jo arrived by bus and followed a notice saying the new library was ten minutes away. She soon discovered that the suggested path crossed a steep hill.
Jo was carrying books and recovering from a knee injury. She phoned the library rather than continue along a difficult route. A librarian explained that a level path followed the river, although it was slightly longer. It ended beside the school’s side gate, which remained open during library hours.
Jo followed this alternative and arrived comfortably. She suggested that future notices mention both routes instead of describing the quickest one as suitable for everybody. The librarian thanked her and added a short accessibility note to the website. The temporary building had not become closer, but clearer information allowed visitors to choose a route according to their needs rather than discover important difficulties halfway through the journey.

listening.teaching: If you are joining today’s town walk, please meet outside the old post office at ten. The bridge near the market is closed, so do not follow last year’s printed route. We will use the riverside path instead. It is level, but part of it may be wet after the morning rain. Please wear suitable shoes. The walk will finish at the community garden, where a volunteer can explain the planting project. Anyone wishing to return directly to the starting point can leave the group at the library corner. Let the guide know before doing so, because we need to keep an accurate count of participants.
listening.test: Welcome to the university open day. Visitors arriving from the bus stop should follow the blue arrows towards the main courtyard. The red arrows lead to student accommodation tours, which begin later. If you need a step-free entrance, continue past the courtyard and use the door beside the café. It may look like a staff entrance, but it is open to all visitors today. The information desk is inside on the left. A shuttle minibus can take people to the sports building on request, though it does not run to a fixed timetable. Please ask at the desk rather than wait outside and hope it will arrive.

questions.prompt: Why did the helper ask about access needs?
options: The crossing lights were out of order.
The museum was closing earlier.
The nearest route included steps.
questions.answer: The nearest route included steps.
questions.explanation: 最近不等于无台阶。

questions.prompt: Why check the website?
options: To check the ticket price at the gate.
Construction might have changed the entrance.
To find a faster taxi route.
questions.answer: Construction might have changed the entrance.
questions.explanation: 核查临时通行变化。

questions.prompt: Why not follow the old printed walk route?
options: A bridge is closed.
The riverside path has disappeared.
The market opens at a different time.
questions.answer: A bridge is closed.
questions.explanation: 明确桥梁关闭。

questions.prompt: What should someone leaving early do?
options: Return to the start without telling anyone.
Give the map to another visitor first.
Tell the guide.
questions.answer: Tell the guide.
questions.explanation: 领队需保持准确人数。

questions.prompt: Why did Jo phone the library?
options: She could not find any current opening hours.
The suggested route was physically difficult for her.
The bus had stopped at the old building.
questions.answer: The suggested route was physically difficult for her.
questions.explanation: 受伤膝盖和携书使陡坡困难。

questions.prompt: What change did Jo recommend?
options: Mentioning both quick and accessible routes.
Only describing the quickest route more briefly.
Replacing the river path with a bus timetable.
questions.answer: Mentioning both quick and accessible routes.
questions.explanation: 让来访者按需求选路。

questions.prompt: Which entrance is step-free?
options: The main courtyard entrance before the café.
The red-arrow accommodation entrance.
The door beside the café beyond the courtyard.
questions.answer: The door beside the café beyond the courtyard.
questions.explanation: 无台阶入口在院子后咖啡馆旁。

questions.prompt: How should visitors arrange the shuttle?
options: Wait outside for a half-hourly departure.
Ask at the information desk.
Request it from the accommodation guide later.
questions.answer: Ask at the information desk.
questions.explanation: 小巴按要求提供，无固定班次。

writing.prompt: Write directions to a public building. Include a landmark, an access warning and an alternative route.
checklist: 回应题目要求，包含具体情境与明确目的。
用段落或清楚顺序组织信息，补充必要原因。
检查时态、指代及词语搭配，避免影响理解的错误。
核对内容是否由自己独立组织，并说明信息的来源。

speaking.prompt: Give directions, then check that your partner understands the important turns and conditions.
followups: Why would that choice suit this situation?
What difficulty might occur?
How would you explain the situation to someone who disagrees?

interaction.twist: 最近路线有台阶，较长路线没有台阶但部分路面可能湿滑。

finalModules.title: 结识新朋友与维持对话
finalModules.focus: 自然追问、分享经历、尊重不愿展开的话题

vocab.head: introduce
vocab.example: At a neighbourhood meal, our host helped introduce people who had recently moved into the same apartment building.
vocab.exampleZh: 在邻里聚餐上，主人帮忙介绍刚搬进同栋公寓的人。

vocab.head: interest
vocab.example: I asked a neighbour about an interest she mentioned rather than immediately asking personal questions about her salary.
vocab.exampleZh: 我询问邻居提过的兴趣，而非马上打听私人薪水。

vocab.head: mention
vocab.example: She happened to mention photography, which gave me an easy way to continue the conversation without changing topics.
vocab.exampleZh: 她恰好提到摄影，让我能不换话题自然继续。

vocab.head: recently
vocab.example: She had recently joined a weekend walking group and was learning to photograph birds near the river.
vocab.exampleZh: 她最近加入周末徒步组，正在学拍河边鸟类。

vocab.head: experience
vocab.example: I shared an experience of trying to photograph a kingfisher, including the long wait and the disappointing result.
vocab.exampleZh: 我分享拍翠鸟的经历，包括漫长等候和失望结果。

vocab.head: curious
vocab.example: She was curious about the place, so I explained how to reach it without claiming to be an expert.
vocab.exampleZh: 她对地点好奇，所以我解释怎么到达，但没装专家。

vocab.head: interrupt
vocab.example: When another guest joined us, I paused instead of continuing to interrupt with every detail of my story.
vocab.exampleZh: 另一客人加入时，我停下来，而非不断插入故事细节。

vocab.head: include
vocab.example: We tried to include him by explaining the topic and asking whether he enjoyed any outdoor activities himself.
vocab.exampleZh: 我们解释话题，问他是否喜欢户外活动，让他参与。

vocab.head: prefer
vocab.example: He said he preferred indoor hobbies, so we did not pressure him to join a walk he clearly disliked.
vocab.exampleZh: 他说更喜欢室内爱好，所以我们没逼他参加明显不喜欢的徒步。

vocab.head: suggest
vocab.example: Instead, he suggested a local exhibition where photographs of the river would be displayed the following month.
vocab.exampleZh: 他反而建议去当地展览，下月将展出河流照片。

vocab.head: invitation
vocab.example: His invitation gave us another chance to meet, but we checked dates before promising that everybody could attend.
vocab.exampleZh: 他的邀请让我们有机会再见，不过承诺所有人出席前先核对日期。

vocab.head: contact
vocab.example: We exchanged contact details with permission and ended the conversation without expecting an immediate friendship from one pleasant meeting.
vocab.exampleZh: 我们经同意交换联系方式，不指望一次愉快见面就立刻成为好友。

sourceA.title: 结识新朋友与维持对话：教学情境
sourceA.text: At a neighbourhood meal, our host helped introduce people who had recently moved into the same apartment building. I asked a neighbour about an interest she mentioned rather than immediately asking personal questions about her salary. She happened to mention photography, which gave me an easy way to continue the conversation without changing topics. She had recently joined a weekend walking group and was learning to photograph birds near the river. I shared an experience of trying to photograph a kingfisher, including the long wait and the disappointing result. She was curious about the place, so I explained how to reach it without claiming to be an expert. When another guest joined us, I paused instead of continuing to interrupt with every detail of my story. We tried to include him by explaining the topic and asking whether he enjoyed any outdoor activities himself. He said he preferred indoor hobbies, so we did not pressure him to join a walk he clearly disliked. Instead, he suggested a local exhibition where photographs of the river would be displayed the following month. His invitation gave us another chance to meet, but we checked dates before promising that everybody could attend. We exchanged contact details with permission and ended the conversation without expecting an immediate friendship from one pleasant meeting.

sourceB.title: A conversation at a language exchange
sourceB.text:
At her first language exchange, Mei sat beside a retired engineer called Paul. She had prepared questions about jobs, but Paul gave short answers and looked uncomfortable. Instead of asking another work question, Mei asked what had brought him to the event. He explained that he wanted to speak with visitors before volunteering at a local museum.
This gave them a more interesting topic. Mei asked which part of the museum he liked most, and Paul described a collection of old bicycles. She shared a memory of repairing a bicycle with her grandfather. Their conversation became easier because both people had something relevant to contribute.
When the organiser asked participants to change partners, Paul offered to continue chatting after the next event. Mei accepted without feeling that she had to share her phone number immediately. They agreed to meet at the same table the following week. She realised that successful conversation did not mean completing a prepared list of questions. It meant noticing the other person’s response and choosing a direction that both people were comfortable exploring.

listening.teaching: Hello everyone. At tonight’s international supper, you will begin at the table number printed on your card. After the main course, we will invite you to move, so you can meet a different group over dessert. There is no need to deliver a formal introduction. A simple question about a favourite local place is usually enough to begin. Please avoid assuming that everyone wants to discuss their job or country’s politics. If someone gives a short answer, offer another topic rather than asking the same question more loudly. You are welcome to exchange contact details, but ask first before adding anyone to a group chat or posting photographs of them.
listening.test: I used to worry that a conversation would fail if there was a pause. At a community cooking class, I filled every silence with another question. Later, a classmate told me she had been trying to think of the right word and needed a moment. I began leaving more space and sharing small experiences of my own instead of interviewing everyone. The conversations became more balanced. I still ask questions, but I try to respond to the answer before moving on. A good exchange is not a competition to avoid silence; both people need time to understand, contribute and decide how much they want to share.

questions.prompt: How did photography help the conversation?
options: It allowed the speaker to give professional advice.
It showed that all neighbours would enjoy walking.
It provided a shared topic for follow-up.
questions.answer: It provided a shared topic for follow-up.
questions.explanation: 从已提兴趣追问。

questions.prompt: How was the new guest included?
options: He was invited to join the walk before explaining his interests.
The topic was explained and his interests were invited.
He was asked to wait until the story ended.
questions.answer: The topic was explained and his interests were invited.
questions.explanation: 让对方有可参与的入口。

questions.prompt: When do supper guests change groups?
options: After the main course.
Before the main course begins.
Only after the final announcement.
questions.answer: After the main course.
questions.explanation: 甜点阶段换桌。

questions.prompt: What requires permission?
options: Moving to the next table.
Asking about a local favourite place.
Adding someone to a group chat.
questions.answer: Adding someone to a group chat.
questions.explanation: 隐私与分享需先同意。

questions.prompt: Why did Mei change topic?
options: She wanted to complete the prepared job questions faster.
Paul seemed uncomfortable answering work questions.
Paul had already asked to leave the event.
questions.answer: Paul seemed uncomfortable answering work questions.
questions.explanation: 注意对方反馈而非照清单。

questions.prompt: What did they agree for later?
options: Meeting at the same table the following week.
Exchanging phone numbers before changing partners.
Visiting the museum immediately after the event.
questions.answer: Meeting at the same table the following week.
questions.explanation: 明确保留联系方式界限。

questions.prompt: Why did the classmate need a pause?
options: She wanted to change to a different class.
She had not understood the activity instructions.
She was finding the right word.
questions.answer: She was finding the right word.
questions.explanation: 停顿不等于交流失败。

questions.prompt: What made the exchange more balanced?
options: Asking the same question again more quickly.
Leaving space and sharing relevant experiences.
Avoiding sharing any personal experience.
questions.answer: Leaving space and sharing relevant experiences.
questions.explanation: 双向贡献取代采访式连问。

writing.prompt: Write an informal message inviting someone you met recently to an activity. Give relevant details and make it easy to decline.
checklist: 回应题目要求，包含具体情境与明确目的。
用段落或清楚顺序组织信息，补充必要原因。
检查时态、指代及词语搭配，避免影响理解的错误。
核对内容是否由自己独立组织，并说明信息的来源。

speaking.prompt: Start a conversation, follow one answer with a relevant question and respond naturally to a change of topic.
followups: Why would that choice suit this situation?
What difficulty might occur?
How would you explain the situation to someone who disagrees?

interaction.goal: 找到双方都愿意聊的话题并提出不过度施压的再见面邀请。
interaction.twist: 一方不愿讨论工作，且不能参加最初建议的活动。

delayed.readingPrompt: At least fourteen days later, read a new account of a similar problem. Identify its purpose, two important details and one difference from this module.
delayed.writingPrompt: Write a new message about a similar situation with different people and constraints. Do not reuse the original wording.
delayed.speakingPrompt: Explain a fresh solution to a partner, then answer two unexpected follow-up questions without a script.

assessmentWriting.prompt: Write an informal follow-up to someone met at a language exchange. Suggest meeting again without demanding private contact details.
checklist: 包含陌生情境要求的信息与明确目的。
给出具体理由或条件，不照搬教学任务的答案。
组织顺序清楚，检查指代、时态与礼貌程度。
独立完成并保留原稿，交给伙伴或教师核对是否易懂。

assessmentSpeaking.prompt: Respond to a partner who gives brief answers about work by moving naturally to another mutually comfortable topic.
followups: Which condition matters most in this particular situation?
What would you ask before agreeing?
How would you respond if the other person suggested a different solution?

finalModules.title: 学习计划与反馈
finalModules.focus: 把目标转成可执行活动，用反馈调整方法

vocab.head: goal
vocab.example: When Luis began evening classes, his goal was to discuss simple work problems rather than collect perfect exercise scores.
vocab.exampleZh: Luis 开始夜校时，目标是讨论简单工作问题，而非收集完美习题分数。

vocab.head: schedule
vocab.example: His schedule included twenty minutes after breakfast, a time that was easier to protect than late evening study.
vocab.exampleZh: 他安排早餐后学二十分钟，比深夜学习更容易保证。

vocab.head: manage
vocab.example: He could manage short reading tasks, but he often postponed speaking because nobody was available to practise with him.
vocab.exampleZh: 他能完成短阅读，却因无人陪练常推迟口语。

vocab.head: record
vocab.example: His teacher suggested that he record a short explanation first and listen for places where the meaning became unclear.
vocab.exampleZh: 老师建议先录简短解释，听哪些地方意思变不清。

vocab.head: feedback
vocab.example: Useful feedback came from a partner who identified one confusing sentence instead of listing every small mistake at once.
vocab.exampleZh: 有用反馈来自同伴指出一句难懂的话，而非一次列全部小错。

vocab.head: improve
vocab.example: Luis tried to improve that sentence by adding a clear reason and replacing a word he did not fully understand.
vocab.exampleZh: Luis 加清楚理由并替换不完全理解的词，改善那句话。

vocab.head: progress
vocab.example: He checked his progress with a new topic a week later rather than repeating the same answer until it sounded smooth.
vocab.exampleZh: 一周后他用新主题检查进展，而非反复同一答案至流畅。

vocab.head: habit
vocab.example: The habit of reviewing a little each day helped him remember phrases that he had previously forgotten after class.
vocab.exampleZh: 每天稍复习的习惯让他记住以前下课就忘的短语。

vocab.head: challenge
vocab.example: An unexpected question remained a challenge, so he practised asking people to clarify what they wanted to know.
vocab.exampleZh: 意外问题仍是挑战，所以他练习请人澄清想知道什么。

vocab.head: realistic
vocab.example: A realistic plan also allowed breaks when family responsibilities made study difficult, instead of treating every missed session as failure.
vocab.exampleZh: 现实计划也在家庭责任使学习困难时允许休息，不把每次缺课当失败。

vocab.head: adjust
vocab.example: He would adjust the following week’s workload without trying to complete several hours of exercises in one tired evening.
vocab.exampleZh: 他调整下周任务量，不在疲惫晚间赶数小时习题。

vocab.head: independent
vocab.example: By the end of term, an independent conversation showed which parts of his learning had become useful beyond the classroom.
vocab.exampleZh: 学期末独立对话显示哪些学习已能在课堂外使用。

sourceA.title: 学习计划与反馈：教学情境
sourceA.text: When Luis began evening classes, his goal was to discuss simple work problems rather than collect perfect exercise scores. His schedule included twenty minutes after breakfast, a time that was easier to protect than late evening study. He could manage short reading tasks, but he often postponed speaking because nobody was available to practise with him. His teacher suggested that he record a short explanation first and listen for places where the meaning became unclear. Useful feedback came from a partner who identified one confusing sentence instead of listing every small mistake at once. Luis tried to improve that sentence by adding a clear reason and replacing a word he did not fully understand. He checked his progress with a new topic a week later rather than repeating the same answer until it sounded smooth. The habit of reviewing a little each day helped him remember phrases that he had previously forgotten after class. An unexpected question remained a challenge, so he practised asking people to clarify what they wanted to know. A realistic plan also allowed breaks when family responsibilities made study difficult, instead of treating every missed session as failure. He would adjust the following week’s workload without trying to complete several hours of exercises in one tired evening.

sourceB.title: Preparing for a practical test
sourceB.text:
Asha was learning to drive and could complete familiar routes confidently. She assumed that doing the same route more quickly meant she was ready for the practical test. Her instructor noticed that she became uncertain whenever roadworks changed a lane or a sign appeared in an unexpected place.
They revised the lesson plan. Instead of repeating only the test area, they used unfamiliar roads and practised explaining why a particular decision was safe. Asha also kept a short record of situations she found difficult. This helped her distinguish a missing rule from a moment of distraction.
Some lessons felt less successful because she made more mistakes on new roads. The instructor explained that these mistakes provided information that familiar practice could hide. After two weeks, Asha revisited one of the difficult situations and handled it more calmly.
She did not take the improvement as proof that every driving skill was secure. She used it to choose what to practise next. Her revised plan combined familiar practice for confidence with unfamiliar situations that required attention and independent judgement, making progress more meaningful than speed on a single known route.

listening.teaching: Our study group meets on Tuesday evenings, but you do not have to prepare a perfect presentation. Bring a short account of something you tried to learn and one question about a difficulty you faced. We will work in pairs before sharing ideas with the whole group. Please give specific feedback, such as identifying a point that needs an example, rather than saying only that a talk was good or bad. Nobody is required to show private grades or personal records. If you miss a meeting, use the summary on our noticeboard to choose one small activity for the next week. You do not need to complete everybody else’s tasks as punishment for being absent.
listening.test: I changed my revision method after noticing that colourful notes took most of my study time. They looked organised, but I could not explain the ideas without looking at them. Now I close the book and write a short answer from memory before checking what I missed. I still make notes, though I keep them brief. Once a week, a friend asks me a new question using the same topic. This is harder than copying a page, and the result is sometimes disappointing. However, it tells me what I can actually use. I judge the method by later recall rather than by how attractive my notebook looks.

questions.prompt: Why study after breakfast?
options: It was the only time a partner was available.
Morning tasks earned extra class marks.
That time was easier to protect.
questions.answer: That time was easier to protect.
questions.explanation: 根据可持续时间而非表面时长规划。

questions.prompt: How was progress checked?
options: By making the original recording smoother.
With a new topic after a delay.
By increasing the length of the vocabulary list.
questions.answer: With a new topic after a delay.
questions.explanation: 迁移与延迟比熟练复述更有信息。

questions.prompt: What should group members bring?
options: A learning experience and a question about a difficulty.
A finished presentation with no mistakes.
A list of everyone else’s study tasks.
questions.answer: A learning experience and a question about a difficulty.
questions.explanation: 任务为经历与问题，不要求完美演讲。

questions.prompt: What feedback is recommended?
options: A judgement that the presentation was simply good.
A comparison of private grades with classmates.
A specific point needing an example.
questions.answer: A specific point needing an example.
questions.explanation: 具体可操作反馈更有用。

questions.prompt: What weakness did unfamiliar roads reveal?
options: Asha was taking familiar routes too slowly.
Uncertainty when the situation changed.
She had forgotten how to record driving lessons.
questions.answer: Uncertainty when the situation changed.
questions.explanation: 熟悉路线隐藏了应变问题。

questions.prompt: Why did more mistakes sometimes help?
options: They revealed needs that familiar practice concealed.
They meant the test could be booked immediately.
They showed that earlier confidence was entirely false.
questions.answer: They revealed needs that familiar practice concealed.
questions.explanation: 错误提供诊断信息，不是直接判失败。

questions.prompt: Why were colourful notes insufficient?
options: The notes contained too few examples.
The speaker used the wrong colour scheme.
The speaker could not explain the ideas without them.
questions.answer: The speaker could not explain the ideas without them.
questions.explanation: 外观组织不等于独立掌握。

questions.prompt: How is the new method judged?
options: By the amount of information copied.
By later recall and use.
By how confidently the friend praised the notes.
questions.answer: By later recall and use.
questions.explanation: 检验真正记忆与使用。

writing.prompt: Write a realistic two-week learning plan. Identify one specific difficulty, a practice activity and a way to check progress.
checklist: 回应题目要求，包含具体情境与明确目的。
用段落或清楚顺序组织信息，补充必要原因。
检查时态、指代及词语搭配，避免影响理解的错误。
核对内容是否由自己独立组织，并说明信息的来源。

speaking.prompt: Explain how you would change a study method that feels easy but produces weak recall.
followups: Why would that choice suit this situation?
What difficulty might occur?
How would you explain the situation to someone who disagrees?

interaction.goal: 根据具体困难选择练习和复核方法。
interaction.twist: 学习者时间减少一半，但仍想维持所有原任务。

delayed.readingPrompt: At least fourteen days later, read a new account of a similar problem. Identify its purpose, two important details and one difference from this module.
delayed.writingPrompt: Write a new message about a similar situation with different people and constraints. Do not reuse the original wording.
delayed.speakingPrompt: Explain a fresh solution to a partner, then answer two unexpected follow-up questions without a script.

assessmentWriting.prompt: Write a revised practice plan for a learner who performs well on familiar driving routes but struggles with unexpected changes.
checklist: 包含陌生情境要求的信息与明确目的。
给出具体理由或条件，不照搬教学任务的答案。
组织顺序清楚，检查指代、时态与礼貌程度。
独立完成并保留原稿，交给伙伴或教师核对是否易懂。

assessmentSpeaking.prompt: Explain how to test whether a new revision method helps recall rather than merely producing attractive notes.
followups: Which condition matters most in this particular situation?
What would you ask before agreeing?
How would you respond if the other person suggested a different solution?

finalModules.title: 工作沟通与任务协调
finalModules.focus: 确认职责、优先事项和截止时间，及时报告困难

vocab.head: task
vocab.example: On my first week at the visitor centre, I received a task to prepare signs for a weekend exhibition.
vocab.exampleZh: 在游客中心第一周，我接到准备周末展览标牌的任务。

vocab.head: responsibility
vocab.example: My responsibility covered the wording, but another colleague would check the facts and arrange the final printing.
vocab.exampleZh: 我负责措辞，另一同事核查事实并安排最终印刷。

vocab.head: deadline
vocab.example: The deadline was Thursday afternoon, although I needed the photographs before I could decide how much text would fit.
vocab.exampleZh: 截止为周四下午，不过我需先有照片才能决定容纳多少文字。

vocab.head: priority
vocab.example: My manager explained that clear directions were the first priority, while background information could be shortened if space was limited.
vocab.exampleZh: 经理说清晰指引优先，背景信息在空间不足时可缩短。

vocab.head: update
vocab.example: I sent a brief update on Tuesday, stating what was finished and which photographs were still missing from the folder.
vocab.exampleZh: 周二我简报已完内容及文件夹仍缺哪些照片。

vocab.head: delay
vocab.example: A delay in one image did not need to stop the whole project, provided we agreed on a temporary layout.
vocab.exampleZh: 只要同意临时版式，一张图片延误不必阻止整个项目。

vocab.head: permission
vocab.example: Before using an older photograph, I asked for permission because I did not know whether its licence covered this exhibition.
vocab.exampleZh: 用旧照片前我请求许可，因为不知道授权是否覆盖本展。

vocab.head: colleague
vocab.example: A colleague suggested a simpler diagram, which communicated the location more clearly than the photograph we had been waiting for.
vocab.exampleZh: 同事建议更简单示意图，比等待中的照片更清楚传达位置。

vocab.head: revise
vocab.example: I could revise the layout that morning, but I needed the fact checker to approve the new labels before printing.
vocab.exampleZh: 我上午能修改版式，但印前需核查人批准新标签。

vocab.head: confirm
vocab.example: We agreed to confirm the final version by email so nobody would accidentally print a draft from the shared folder.
vocab.exampleZh: 我们同意邮件确认最终版，防止误印共享夹草稿。

vocab.head: reliable
vocab.example: Reliable teamwork meant reporting difficulties early rather than promising that everything was fine until the last possible moment.
vocab.exampleZh: 可靠合作意味着及早报困难，而非到最后仍承诺一切正常。

vocab.head: solution
vocab.example: The solution emerged because each person understood the goal, their own role and when another person’s decision was needed.
vocab.exampleZh: 解决办法出现是因为人人懂目标、自身角色及何时需他人决策。

sourceA.title: 工作沟通与任务协调：教学情境
sourceA.text: On my first week at the visitor centre, I received a task to prepare signs for a weekend exhibition. My responsibility covered the wording, but another colleague would check the facts and arrange the final printing. The deadline was Thursday afternoon, although I needed the photographs before I could decide how much text would fit. My manager explained that clear directions were the first priority, while background information could be shortened if space was limited. I sent a brief update on Tuesday, stating what was finished and which photographs were still missing from the folder. A delay in one image did not need to stop the whole project, provided we agreed on a temporary layout. Before using an older photograph, I asked for permission because I did not know whether its licence covered this exhibition. A colleague suggested a simpler diagram, which communicated the location more clearly than the photograph we had been waiting for. I could revise the layout that morning, but I needed the fact checker to approve the new labels before printing. We agreed to confirm the final version by email so nobody would accidentally print a draft from the shared folder. Reliable teamwork meant reporting difficulties early rather than promising that everything was fine until the last possible moment.

sourceB.title: A café changes its rota
sourceB.text:
At a small café, the manager posted next week’s working hours in a group chat. Two assistants replied with a thumbs-up symbol. The manager assumed both had accepted every shift, but one assistant thought the symbol only meant that the message had been received. On Saturday, the café was unexpectedly short of staff.
The team discussed the misunderstanding rather than blaming the assistant immediately. They discovered that availability requests and confirmed shifts had been sent in the same format. Staff could not easily tell whether a reply was asking for a change or accepting a final arrangement.
The manager introduced a simple system. Requests for availability were labelled as drafts. The final rota carried a date and required a written confirmation from each person. Any later change had to name both the original shift and the agreed replacement.
The system took a little more time, but it reduced uncertainty. A symbol was still welcome as a friendly response, yet it no longer counted as agreement to a work commitment. Clear communication meant making the expected action explicit instead of assuming that everyone understood a brief message in exactly the same way.

listening.teaching: Before we open the exhibition, I need each team to check one area. The design group should confirm that every arrow points towards the actual entrance, since the display moved yesterday. The information group should compare dates against the organiser’s final email, not the earlier draft. Please report any problem to me by eleven so we have time to make changes before visitors arrive at noon. Do not replace a printed sign with your own wording without checking it. If the correction is urgent and I am helping a visitor, tell the deputy manager. It is better to identify a small uncertainty now than leave guests following information we already suspect is wrong.
listening.test: Hello, this is your supervisor at the volunteer shop. Tomorrow’s delivery will arrive at ten thirty instead of nine, so you do not need to come in early. Please keep your usual eleven o’clock start unless you have separately agreed to help unload. We still need someone to check the donated books for damaged pages before they go onto the shelves. That task has priority over rearranging the window display. If there are too many books to finish safely, leave a clear note stating what remains rather than rushing through the checks. I will review the unfinished section with the afternoon team and decide how to divide the work.

questions.prompt: Why could one missing image be managed?
options: The printing deadline could be moved until after opening.
The exhibition no longer required the missing label.
A temporary layout could keep other work moving.
questions.answer: A temporary layout could keep other work moving.
questions.explanation: 部分延误不必阻断全部任务。

questions.prompt: Why confirm the final version by email?
options: To request new photographs for the same draft.
To prevent a draft being printed by mistake.
To allow anyone to approve a version independently.
questions.answer: To prevent a draft being printed by mistake.
questions.explanation: 明确版本降低交接错误。

questions.prompt: Which date source should be used?
options: The organiser’s final email.
The first shared draft.
The previous year’s printed brochure.
questions.answer: The organiser’s final email.
questions.explanation: 听力明确最终邮件而非早稿。

questions.prompt: Who can handle an urgent correction if the manager is busy?
options: The design group without any further check.
The visitor who first noticed the mistake.
The deputy manager.
questions.answer: The deputy manager.
questions.explanation: 有明确替代报告路径。

questions.prompt: What did the thumbs-up symbol mean to one assistant?
options: Acceptance of the whole rota.
Receipt of the message, not acceptance of every shift.
A request for a different Saturday shift.
questions.answer: Receipt of the message, not acceptance of every shift.
questions.explanation: 符号被赋予不同交际含义。

questions.prompt: What did the new rota system require?
options: Written confirmation of the final arrangement.
A symbol beneath every availability request.
Confirmation only when a shift is unwanted.
questions.answer: Written confirmation of the final arrangement.
questions.explanation: 最终排班与草案区分并明确接受。

questions.prompt: What is tomorrow’s usual start time?
options: Ten thirty when delivery arrives.
Nine to help unload automatically.
Eleven o’clock.
questions.answer: Eleven o’clock.

sourceA.title: 阅读消息与核对信息：教学情境
sourceA.text: A headline in our neighbourhood group claimed that the swimming pool would close permanently at the end of summer. Before sharing the message, I looked for its source and found that it referred to an old council discussion. The current statement described a temporary closure for repairs, not a decision to remove the pool from the town. There was no evidence in the document for the claim that every member would lose their remaining fees. The temporary arrangement allowed members to use another centre, although they needed to book sessions through a different website. One important detail remained unclear: whether the alternative centre would offer suitable times for people working late shifts. I decided to contact the council directly instead of assuming that a missing detail meant the entire plan was dishonest. Their reply explained that the timetable was still being negotiated and would be published before the repair work began. I shared a short correction that separated the confirmed information from the original claim about permanent closure. I also mentioned the uncertain timetable, because a correction should not pretend that every practical question has already been answered. A reliable summary needed both the date of the statement and a link that neighbours could check for themselves.

sourceB.title: A surprising school result
sourceB.text:
A local website reported that pupils who joined a school chess club achieved higher mathematics marks. Its headline suggested that chess lessons had caused the improvement. The article described the marks accurately, but it did not explain how students had joined the club.
A teacher checked the information and discovered that many club members had already been strong at mathematics before the club opened. They had also volunteered to attend, while other pupils chose music or sport. The comparison therefore could not show what would happen if every student received chess lessons.
The teacher did not conclude that chess was useless. Club members enjoyed the activity, practised concentration and made new friends. These were worthwhile benefits, even if the examination claim was too strong. She asked the website to revise its headline and include the earlier marks.
The edited article described an association rather than a proven cause. Some readers found the new title less exciting, but it gave families a fairer basis for choosing activities. A careful correction preserved the real observations while removing an explanation that the available information could not support.

listening.teaching: This is an update about the road outside the community centre. Yesterday’s message said the road would close for three days. The council has now confirmed that vehicles will be stopped only between nine and four on Monday and Tuesday. Pedestrians can still use the marked pavement, but please follow staff instructions near the work area. Deliveries to the centre should use the rear entrance during those hours. Some messages in the local group describe the centre as closed all week; that is incorrect. Activities inside are continuing. If your event organiser changes a particular session, they will contact you directly. Check the dated notice on our website before making travel arrangements.
listening.test: I saw a photograph online showing an empty shopping street and a message saying that every business had closed. The image looked convincing until I noticed that it had been taken early on a public holiday. I checked several shop websites and found that most were trading normally later that week. One shop had closed, so the message was not completely invented, but it gave a false impression by using a real image without its timing. I posted the opening information without insulting the person who shared it. Correcting the context seemed more useful than starting an argument about whether they were a bad person.
